newsitem.title: SPAIN: Portuguese bonds to gain over bonos at short end.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese bonds to gain over bonos at short end.

text.p: Long term Iberian bonds should be little changed a week from now, restrained ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting, analysts said on Friday.
But at the short end yields may turn in favour of Portugal. "I expect the Portuguese yield curve to steepen in the next few days," said Martin Amaral Neto at Banco Essi in Lisbon.
"I guess the market will start to give increased probability to an official rate cut here," he added.
In Portugal the 6.20 percent key money market rate could be cut soon, after January inflation is announced, analysts said.
The Bank of Spain is expected to cut official rates aggressively this year, but its next move may not be approved that soon, dealers said.
Recent peseta volatility in the foreign exchange market may prompt the central bank to wait a few weeks longer, they said.
The Bank of Spain's key money market rate was last cut by 25 basis points on January 16 to six percent. It started 1996 at nine percent.
This week the peseta hit a low at around 84.70 versus the mark, sharply lower from 83.30 reached at the start of January.

"At the longer end, there is little value..so there is more interest at the front end. But given a much weaker peseta and such sharp movements in short term deposits, we have a very nervous market," a dealer in Madrid said.
At the last Treasury auction, six-month bill yields remained unchanged, after a run of reductions. At the same time Spain's yield curve flattened slightly.
So this week analysts expect Portuguese bonds to be snapped up at the shorter end, where they are still offering a positive margin over their Spanish counterparts.
One year Portuguese bonds offer a yield of around 5.55 percent, almost 20 basis points over Spain, while the three year segment is paying six basis points more.
But at the longer end the 10-year spread over German Bunds should remain unchanged around the current 90 basis points.
"I would not be particularly bullish for the next week," said Mario Vigario at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Lisbon.
"I don't expect the Portuguese market to outperform".
High volatility in both the dollar and in U.S. markets will drive Iberian bonds ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting, where the Fed could approve an increase in official rates.
But what seems to be holding the market back is the possibility the Fed could sit tight until mid-March.

"In the United States there is a higher risk of inflation picking up, and markets are pricing in a rise in official rates although it could came later on," said Thierry Loiseau at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.
Bank of America's chief economist Henrik Lumholdt believes the Federal Reserve will lift rates by 25 basis points in March.
The 10-year spread over Bunds could trade over a week between 82 and 97 basis points, said Loiseau.
"There is a very solid trading range between 82 and 97 basis points and if the Federal Reserve doesn't move rates, we will stay there," he said.
For Portugal, analysts have similar expectations.
"I expect Portuguese bonds to trade at around 85 and 95 basis points over Bunds," said Deutsche Morgan's Vigario.
-- Madrid Newsroom, + 341 585 8340
